During the Iranian Hostage Crisis, Canadian Ambassador Ken Taylor briefs reporters on local conditions the week before smuggling out 6 Americans who he was hiding. Tehran. 1980

The Iran hostage crisis was a diplomatic crisis between Iran and the United States. 52 American diplomats and citizens were held hostage for 444 days (November 4, 1979, to January 20, 1981) after a group of Iranian students took over the U.S. Embassy in Tehran.

Six Americans managed to escape after the students stormed the Embassy. They eventually made their way to the homes of diplomats Ken Taylor and John Sheardown. It was only then that Taylor contacted Ottawa and it was decided to smuggle the six Americans out of Iran on an international flight using Canadian passports. The passports that were issued contained a set of forged Iranian visas prepared by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency.

The CIA enlisted its disguise and exfiltration expert, Tony Mendez, to provide a cover story, documents, appropriate clothing and materials to change their appearance. The cover story had the six being a Hollywood crew scouting movie locations for a film named Argo. After 79 days in hiding, on January 27, 1980, the Americans made it through security at Tehran's airport and boarded a Swissair flight for Zürich, Switzerland. By coincidence, the aircraft was named Aargau.

The 2012 Best Picture Oscar winning film Argo was loosley based upon this rescue.
